A 27 year old democratic socialist just beat the mayor of Providence.

David Morales took 53 percent to Brett Smiley's 46, about 1,700 votes. Smiley outspent him better than three to one and burned a good chunk of it on ads calling Morales soft on police. It didn't work. First sitting mayor in the history of Providence to lose a primary.

Now, the easy post here is to tell you to be afraid of the word socialism. I'm not going to do that, because it would let every person in Rhode Island politics off the hook, and they don't deserve it.

Here is what I think actually happened.

Morales ran on rent. On what it costs to keep a roof over your head in this state. He was outspent five to one and he won anyway, on a median donation of about thirty six dollars, because he was talking about the one thing people are drowning in and the establishment was handing out press releases about how well things are going.

You cannot beat that with a warning label. You beat it with a better answer.

Now let's be honest about the other half.

Morales is a member of the Democratic Socialists of America. That organization's platform is public and it is not moderate. Abolishing ICE. Legal status for people here illegally. Abolishing the Senate. Restructuring the Supreme Court. Deep cuts to the Pentagon. And yes, language on moving toward the abolition of policing and prisons, which Morales himself disavowed during the campaign and says he wants more officers, not fewer.

I'll take him at his word on that. But the platform is still the platform, and it is the organizing document of the movement that just won Rhode Island's capital city.

So here's my honest read.

That result is not a warning about Providence. It's a warning about all of us. When people are squeezed hard enough for long enough, they stop asking whether an idea is radical and start asking whether anybody is offering anything at all.

Sixty years of one party running this state produced the highest electric bills in the country, rents nobody can carry and kids who move away. Voters are not going to keep waiting politely.

If we want to beat this, we have to be the ones with a real answer on what it costs to live here. Not a slogan about socialism. An answer.

That's the whole reason I'm running.
